create.title: Frozen exact M2 global second moment
create.statement_tex: Let I be an interval of length V, 1<=H<=D, D_D be any subset of [c_0D,c_1D] intersected with the positive integers, and |w_D(d)|<=1. For the exact two-sided coefficient beta_(h,H)=-Phi(|h|/(H+1))chi_4(|h|)1_(h odd)/(pi|h|), the frozen block S_(D,H,w)(t)=sum_(0<|h|<=H)beta_(h,H)sum_(d in D_D)w_D(d)e(ht/(4d)) satisfies int_I|S_(D,H,w)(t)|^2dt <<_(c_0,c_1) (V+D^2)D. Exact equal rational frequencies h/d=a/b are grouped before separation; their total coefficient ell2 mass is O(D), and distinct reduced frequencies a/(4b) are separated by a constant times D^(-2). For I=[Y,2Y] and D<=Y^(1/2), the exceptional set at height Y^(1/4+eta) has measure << D Y^(1/2-2eta), and a geometric all-D union has measure <<Y^(1-2eta). The actual h=+-1 no-multiplicity zone has coefficient energy >>D on a nondegenerate full shell, so the diagonal scale is sharp. This is a global metric lemma, not a pointwise or canonical-core estimate.
create.next_action: Use this as the frozen metric kernel and as the base estimate in the exact moving-profile theorem. Do not infer a prescribed-point estimate.

create.title: Exact moving M1 and M2 main-block global second moments
create.statement_tex: Let Y>=2, let D<<sqrt(Y), and use either literal M1 or M2 Vaaler coefficients with both signs. For a fixed compactly supported BV denominator profile at scale D, an arbitrary measurable comparable scale R(t)~D, a height H(t) whose range on [Y,2Y] is fixed-ratio comparable (including H(t)=floor(Dt^(-1/4)) and the accepted dyadic floor), every moving prefix, hard top, and fixed endpoint-star convention satisfy int_Y^(2Y)|S_(i,D)^mov(t)|^2dt <<_epsilon Y^epsilon(Y+D^2)D, i=1,2. The proof uses gamma_(h,r)=beta_(h,r)-beta_(h,r-1) with |gamma_(h,r)|<<r^(-2)1_(|h|<=r), exact interval ray energy O(N/r^2), a binary-prefix maximal separated-frequency inequality, and a Stieltjes decomposition of fixed BV profiles. For D_j=2^(-j)sqrt(Y), weights W(d/(2D_j))1_(d<=floor(sqrt(t))), and bottom eta(d/(2D_(J+1))), J maximal with D_J>=(2Y)^(1/4), the partition is exact and all moving floors and hard endpoints are retained. Only logarithmic losses occur. Arbitrary bounded t-dependent weights are excluded and can violate the target by a factor D.
create.next_action: Use the theorem for global real-variable moments. The remaining bridge is exceptional-set removal at a prescribed point; do not identify this average with either Round-92 canonical core.

create.title: Global real-variable mean square and density-one quarter exponent
create.statement_tex: For every epsilon>0 and Y>=2, P(t)=N(sqrt(t))-pi t satisfies int_Y^(2Y)|P(t)|^2dt <<_epsilon Y^(3/2+epsilon). The exact fixed-in-Y dyadic partition, M9-M1-M2-moving-global-second-moment, the O(Y^(1/4)) pre-Fourier bottom, the accepted pointwise R5-Full residual, and H1-H4 give the assembly. Consequently, for every eta>0, |{t in [Y,2Y]: |P(t)|>Y^(1/4+eta)}| <<_(epsilon,eta) Y^(1-2eta+epsilon), which is density one when epsilon<2eta. This theorem concerns Lebesgue-almost-every real t only; it gives no estimate at a prescribed real or integer t, no jump-point theorem, no bound for either canonical M9 core, and no improvement of the accepted uniform exponent 1/3.
create.next_action: Seek a quantitative local large-value or short-interval theorem that can remove exceptional points without assuming M9-M1 or M9-M2.

The coefficient, support, averaging variable, moving endpoint, and fixed-X norms do not map to either canonical M9 core. The source audit is complete as a non-importable guardrail and creates no implication edge.

The exact moving M2 block has the target global second moment and density-one quarter bound, but the top-scale RMS equals the pointwise target. Remove exceptional points or prove the canonical joint density-discrepancy energy and remaining M2 packets.

reject.reason: A t-dependent bounded denominator weight can conjugate the phases and produce moment of size YD^2, a factor D above the target. Ordered-prefix or fixed-BV motion is essential.
Paying the frozen D^3 term on every height-floor interval loses Y^(1/4) at D=Y^(1/2); the exact height-difference basis is required.
At D=Y^(1/2) and threshold Y^(1/4), the second moment permits exceptional measure O(Y), and the h=+-1 diagonal shows the RMS scale is genuine.
The proof averages over t before the Round-92 transforms and allows every prescribed point to be exceptional. It supplies neither the M1 J^(-1/12) gain nor the M2 rho^(-1/2) gain.

no_change.reason: The global t-average does not estimate the fixed-X four-row Gram operator.
The original-block global moment does not estimate the transformed fixed-X density-discrepancy energy.
The pointwise one-quarter M1 theorem remains open.
The pointwise one-quarter M2 theorem remains open.
Almost-everywhere real-variable control is not endpoint uniformity at every X.
M9 is a uniform pointwise theorem and is not implied by a global second moment.
The bridge still requires pointwise M9 at exponent one quarter.
The new density-one quarter exponent does not improve the accepted uniform one-third exponent or prove the pointwise target.

round_assessment.reason: Round 93 proves the exact frozen and moving M1/M2 global moments, assembles an unconditional real-variable mean square for P, and reaches the quarter exponent on a density-one set with an explicit exceptional-measure exponent, while sharply separating this metric advance from every still-open pointwise core.
